On 8/2/12 11:49 AM, Marco wrote:> Hello,
>
> I am an Italian student currently working on for a Pharma company. I came to know about Stan and I started to read the
> User guide and I found it really interesting. You are really doing a nice job.
> I would love to make a presentation within the company and try to make a comparison with WinBugs.
> From the code available I've seen that there is the folder with the WinBugs examples, but after run some examples and
> get the results, I do not know how to generate some plots within stan.
> Do you have any code complete for make a nice comparison of Stan to WinBugs, with graphs and different times?

This is the wrong group for this discussion.
The stan-dev group is for those working on the
guts of implementing Stan.

This discussion should be on stan-users. There's
a link on the lower lefthand corner of:

http://code.google.com/p/stan/

We're still tweaking the language, so the manual
and syntax are about to change a little bit.

The results are currently being generated by the Stan
program in comma-separated value (CSV) notation.

What do you know how to use? You can read CSV files
into Python, R or Matlab. There are R interfaces to
WinBUGS (like R2WinBUGS) and to JAGS (R2jags).

For Stan, there's a very simple R wrapper that we've tested
on Mac OS X and Linux in the top-level r2stan_sys.R
file. And we're about to release and document a much
richer and more tightly integreated interface.

Stan's strength will be in more complex models (like
ones with hierarchical covariance components) than BUGS.

You probably want to compare effective sample size
divided by time after both implementations have converged.

- Bob
